title: Erdős Problem 626: Erdős's upper bound g_k(n) <= 2 log n / log(k−2) + 1
abstract: For k >= 4 and all sufficiently large n, g_k(n) <= 2 log n / log(k−2) + 1, where g_k(n) is the largest m such that some graph on n vertices with chromatic number k has no cycle of length <= m. This is Erdős's upper bound (Mathematika 1962, Theorem 1) in the form his printed proof gives. Erdős's g_k(n) is the largest girth, one more than the g_k(n) used here, so the formal bound is one weaker than Theorem 1 as printed. With Erdős's lower bound of order log n, it shows that g_k(n) has order log n. Whether g_k(n)/log n converges is the open Erdős Problem 626.
